name: legacy-v5-refit
description: The v5 final refit rebuild_all.py hard-coded as SHIPPING_RECIPES['v5'] until 2026-10-09, verbatim, plus the --epochs 80 it passed by default.
notes: Not measured: no seed panel ran on this flag set, and its reported metrics are in-sample. --phase final-refit fits every row, val and test included, and until 2026-10-09 the report labelled its held-out recall, CQS and promote verdict 'selection_holdout' [training#0]. It now says metrics_source 'in_sample_refit', and composite_score.should_promote refuses it. With --val-every 10 and --checkpoint-metric cqs the restored epoch is also chosen by val recall on rows the model trained on.

--epochs 80 is not in SHIPPING_RECIPES: it was rebuild_all.py's EPOCHS_DEFAULT and train.sh's EPOCHS_REFIT. It is here because rebuild_all.py now passes --epochs only when asked (--epochs, --quick 40, --full 150), so --recipe legacy-v5-refit still trains what the old default run trained.

Against what train.sh passed before it became a wrapper over rebuild_all.py (645e153b): train.sh's v5 refit also passed --hard-neg-boost 0.3, which this recipe leaves at the 0.4 default (a different training run), and --val-every 10, which is the default (no difference). Both passed --batch 512 --seed 7 and no --device, so both trained on cpu. The wrapper dropped the 0.3 without saying so; a reviewer found it.

Against the measure recipe it differs in almost every knob: --dim 48 against 64, NCE 0.7/0.3 against 0.65/0.35, --phase final-refit against select, --era-align procrustes, --robust-scaling, and validation every 10 epochs with the cqs checkpoint against none [orchestration#3, training#6].
